- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, apply a lag correction: subtract 1–3 days of forecasted overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, apply mean reversion bias: pull forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., high → low or vice versa), adjust forecast slope to match sentiment trend direction.  
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 18-day low unless sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and confirmed by 3 consecutive low readings.
